item.description:
↓ Download as PDF
Ziming Zheng
Senior Software Engineer at Atlassian
📧 z.zheng1@unswalumni.com  ·  🔗 linkedin.com/in/zimingzheng
🇦🇺 Australian citizen  ·  📍 Sydney, Australia or remote
About Me
Senior Software Engineer with 6+ years of experience at Atlassian, specializing in large-scale distributed systems and cloud infrastructure. Maintained critical services with 99.99+% availability, and delivering significant cost optimizations. Strong technical leadership demonstrated through mentoring, cross-functional collaboration, and driving complex migration projects. Passionate about building reliable, scalable systems while maintaining operational excellence and customer trust. Increasingly leveraging agentic engineering tools including Atlassian Rovo Dev to amplify delivery.
Experience
Senior Software Engineer — Atlassian Jan 2020 — April 2026
Joined as a graduate engineer in 2020, promoted to mid level in 2022 and to senior level in 2026.
Team 1: Jira Issue Backend Oct 2022 — April 2026
Jira is an issue and project tracking software serving millions of customers worldwide.
  • Leading a sharding data migration project to make Issue Service the single source of truth for all Jira issue data types, a significant milestone in the Jira Monolith decomposition. Designing the end-to-end migration plan based on tenant data shape and environments, and scaling service traffic by more than 8× in 2025 while maintaining SLO targets through proactive monitoring of DynamoDB capacities.
  • Contributing to Jira Monolith decomposition and issue data migration from PostgreSQL to Issue Service (a new micro service) backed by DynamoDB.
    • Driving projects of various issue custom fields migration.
    • Maintaining Issue Service to uphold 99.999% availability on Issue Read Success Rate & 99.99% on other SLOs.
  • Upholding 99.99% availability for critical Jira Issue Read REST & GraphQL APIs backed by Issue Service, with over 2 billion real-customer requests per day in production.
  • Keep The Lights On: maintaining and contributing into decades-old Jira Monolith codebase.
  • Troubleshooting and providing developer support for Enterprise and Premium customers, ensuring high customer satisfaction, data privacy, and trust on Jira Cloud. Collaborating with Customer Support teams.
  • Mentoring new team members. Helping Atlassian recruit talents as a seasoned technical interviewer.
Team 2 Secondment: Cloud Operational Savings Oct 2024 — Mar 2025
  • Led a project to identify and migrate MegaCloud tenants to shared RDS instances through analysis of database performance metrics, in collaboration with Jira SRE.
  • Reduced annual operational costs by ~$500k through right-sizing MegaCloud RDS instances.
Team 3: Cloud Infrastructure Jan 2020 — Oct 2022
  • Contributed to Atlassian's service-to-service network, providing platform solutions including routing, authentication, rate limiting and more.
    • Maintained configurations of Envoy Proxy (an open-source proxy written in C++) for 2,000+ Atlassian micro services powering Jira, Confluence and other Atlassian products.
    • Contributed to an in-house configuration sidecar written in Go, wrapping Envoy proxy (Service Proxy).
  • Led a project of 2 engineers to build new platform-agnostic APIs to enable multi-platform support for Service Proxy provisioning.
    • Extracted Service Proxy provisioning code from the Atlassian internal AWS deployment platform.
    • Built a new service written in TypeScript, from scratch to production, with 99.99% availability, handling about 500 deployment events per day on both AWS EC2 and Kubernetes platforms.
    • Collaborated with cross-functional teams, to address compliance-related challenges such as FedRAMP, enabling Atlassian cloud migrations for customers in government entities.
Software Engineer Intern — CSIRO Data61 Nov 2018 — Feb 2019
  • Built a prototype to migrate CSIRO Workspace Windows Desktop applications written in C++ to a web service from scratch.
    • Designed a Node.js REST API server and an Angular frontend that calls those APIs.
    • The APIs are powered by Node.js C++ addons, which translate Workspace C++ libraries into JavaScript/TypeScript modules.
  • Owned a non-trivial maintenance task to remove the legacy code for an online drag-and-drop user interface written in TypeScript.
    • Managed to upgrade the entire frontend framework from AngularJS to Angular 2, which required extensive architectural modifications.
Academic Tutor — UNSW Sydney 2018 — 2019
  • Conducted tutorials for approximately 25 students each, providing tutoring object-oriented design (OOD) in Java.
  • Created onboarding documentation with examples for JavaFX application development. This documentation was intended for the entire cohort of approximately 500 students who were enrolled in the OOD course each term.
Education
B.Sc. Computer Science with Distinction — UNSW Sydney 2016 — 2019
Activities
Jane Street eTrading Hackathon — In March 2018, a team of 4 developed a bot for maximizing profit through exchanging financial derivatives in simulated markets.
IoT Project: Body Motion Tracking System — In November 2018, a team of 3 built an Android app to track human body motion using TI Sensortag CC2650 with real-time 3D visualization on body movements. I designed the 3D visualization and implemented data bindings between sensors and the 3D model. See more in the project profile link.
Reference
Contact details available upon request

item.title: Customise markdown preview enhanced plugin in vscode
item.description:
Step 1:

Download vscode markdown preview enhanced plugin in vscode

Step 2:

On Ubuntu, use shortcut Ctrl + Shift + p to enable vscode command.

Step 3:

Type to search “Markdown Preview Enhanced: Customize CSS” command

Step 4:

Then it will open a css file called style.less. Next, just copy the css setting below into that file. That’s it and save the file!

/* Please visit the URL below for more information: */
/*   https://shd101wyy.github.io/markdown-preview-enhanced/#/customize-css */
.markdown-preview.markdown-preview {
  // modify your style here
  background-color: rgb(48, 49, 49);
  font-size: 19px;
  p>code, li>code {
    background: rgb(58, 59, 59);
    color: white;
    border-radius: 3px;
    border: 1px;
  }
}

item.title: All about cpp
item.description:
Week 1

Wed

  • community: #include <c++>
  • quick links:
    • https://abseil.io/
    • https://www.stroustrup.com/index.html
  • const
    • auto const course_code = std:string("COMP6771") The whole string is constant
    • If the const is on string builder, the string that is appended everytime is constant
    • const is always on the right
  • string comparision and assignment
    • != to compare two string literal values not reference of string (unlike Java)
    • The slide mentions C++ value semantics

Thurs

  • The compiler we’re using: clang++-11 hello.cpp -o hello
  • clang++-11 -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -std=c++20 -stdlib=libc++ -o hello_test hello.cpp hello_test.cpp
  • This course is using CMake, clang-tidy. Chris had some demos on how to use the test framework in the first 30 mins of lecture
  • Type conversion
    • narrow(lossy) conversion, for example int => bool
  • Default arguments
    • std::string rgb(short r = 0, short g = 0, short b = 0);
  • Two librarys learnt:
    • https://github.com/gsl-lite/gsl-lite
    • https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp
  • We read backwards: a reference to a const integer i auto i = 1; auto const& ref = i;
  • benchmark library: https://github.com/google/benchmark
  • cpp reference &
    • Don’t need to use -> to access elements
    • Can’t be null
    • You can’t change what they refer to once set

Week 2 - need to be revisited

Wed

  • Iterator avoids losing track of container 
    auto playing_card = ranges::find(hand, blue_number);
REQUIRE(playing_card != hand.end());
CHECK(*playing_card == blue_number);

playing_card = hand.erase(playing_card); // we remove a card from our hand when we play it
REQUIRE(playing_card != hand.end());
CHECK(*playing_card == green_draw_two);
    The erase() function returns a new iterator to update the new position in the container. This is because when vector shrinks, the memory will change. If you don’t use the new iterator, the old one may point to null. 
    auto playing_card = ranges::find(hand, blue_number);
REQUIRE(playing_card != hand.end());
CHECK(*playing_card == blue_number);

hand.push_back(green_draw_two);
card_to_play = ranges::find(hand, blue_number)
    Same reason as above. When vector expands, the memory will change. We need to re-find the element and the find() will return an updated new iterator.
  • erase function we saw in this course
    • vector.erase(iterator)
    • std::erase(vector, element)

  • Lambda function need to revisit!!

  • static program analysis: clang-tidy
  • link: just to understand iterator pattern

Thurs

  • More on vector: need to revisit later!!!

Week 3

Wed

  • copy constructor: given auto v2 = std::vector<int>{}
    • auto v3 = v2;
    • auto v3 = std::vector<int>(v2);
    • They are the same.
  • In a C++ class, if access modifier is not specified, the method is private by default.
  • Definition of class initialiser: double salary = 1200.5; in the class
  • There is a benefit of constructor initialiser list and uniform intialisation: Initialiser lists and uniform initialisation avoid having to construct an object once, and then reassign it to a different value after construction. It is more efficient, and for some types, you will not be able to compile without it. 
    class person {
public:
    person()
    : age_{99} { // This is ok!
        /* age_ = 20  (Compile Error!!) */
    }
    auto get_age() -> int const&;
private:
    int const age_ = 18;
};
    • If the private variable is defined in const auto const age_ = 18;, then the const value can be overwritten by constructor initialiser list but can’t be written by the assignment in the constructor.

Thurs

  • explicit keyword to disable implicit conversion.
  • const object can only call const method functions, but const method can be called in any object.
    • There is an exception: using mutable keyword
  • static auto valid_name(std::string const& name) -> bool is a static method in cpp.
    • Rule of thumb: you can use static method whenever that method doesn’t require any class variables.
  • static class variable
    • Rule of thumb: you may use it to define some constants associated with class for example std::string::npods.
  • inline static variable
    • static int MAX_LENGTH_NUM = 20 - You declared the variable but haven’t defined it yet. To make it work: inline static int MAX_LENGTH_NUM = 20
    • The definition can appear in multiple files, what inline means the compiler will pick up one special file and put definition in only that one file. In our case, MAX_LENGTH_NUM is defined once but is declared many times.
    • More inline ref: https://www.quora.com/What-are-the-use-cases-of-inline-variables-introduced-in-C++17
    • Q: Why static int const MAX_LENGth_NUM = 20 doesn’t work?
      • A: Compiler error: C++ forbids in-class initialization of non-const static member
      • A: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/9656941/why-cant-i-initialize-non-const-static-member-or-static-array-in-class/9657064
  • copying constructor is a default thing that cpp compiler is able to do though the user doesn’t write the constructor with the copying paratemeter explicitly. 
    auto a = intvec{}
auto b = intvec{a}
  • intvec() = default defines default constructor. Note that intvec() is a constructor.
  • intvec() = delete It is to prevent copy constructor when it is called implicitly. For example, when the calling function has “passed-by-value” parameter.
    • ref: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zWG0K_c7fI4
  • friend will be used in operator+,-, *, /, %, <<-like operator overloading for example friend point operator+(point const& lhs, point const& rhs).
    • please put the friend operators implementation in class definition (header file)
    • Q: why we need to have friend ???
    • A: for example interface - friend method can cache the values the interface provides
  • Operator overloading - It is “overloading” so any return type and parameter type should be fine. However, it has special meaning to use reference or whether to be friend or object memeber. However, you can do anything doesn’t mean you should do anything.
  • for operator+=-like operator overloading for example 
    point point::operator+=(point const& p) {
    x_ += p.x_;
    y_ += p.y_;
    return *this;
}
    • It is class method because the current object this has meaning on it, whereas, operator+,-,*,/,%,<<-like, there is no current object involved and therefore, we use friend.
  • Miscs
    • [[nodiscard]] to let compiler give warnings if the return value from a function(struct) isn’t handled in the caller function.
    • A noexcept specification on a function is merely a method for a programmer to inform the compiler whether or not a function should throw exceptions.
      • car::~car() noexcept;

Week 4

Weds

  • hidden friend functions are functions defined inside class and regular friend functions are functions defined outside class.
  • assignment is p2 = p1 instead of auto p2 = p1. The latter one is doing copy constructor.
  • subscript operator overloading 
    int operator[](int index) const {
    return index == 0 ? x_ : y_;
}
    • This one is for p1[0]
    int& operator[] (int index) {
    return index == 0 ? x_ : y_;
}
    • This one is for p1[0] = 100
  • Why we prefer static_cast? It’s because static_cast is written by programmer and it has clear error message. Otherwise it is compiler generating error message.
  • type conversion operator overloading: it is better to include explicit to force explicit conversion for type conversion operator overloading. 
    explicit operator std::vector<int>() const {
	return std::vector<int>{x_, y_};
}
    • Below is the usage: implicit type conversion is not a good practise because of the behaviour of compiler. 
      std::vector<int> vec = p; // implicit
auto vec = std::vector<int>(p); // explicit
auto vec = static_cast<std::vector<int>>(p); // explicit
  • Compiler Explorer options: x86-64 clang(trunk) -std=c++20 -stdlib=libc++

To explore more later:

  • https://stackoverflow.com/questions/9656941/why-cant-i-initialize-non-const-static-member-or-static-array-in-class/9657064
  • inline variable and function
  • "hadyen"s
  • mutable keyword
  • hidden friend in cpp (friend function is private) https://www.justsoftwaresolutions.co.uk/cplusplus/hidden-friends.html#:~:text=Rules%20for%20Visibility%20of%20Hidden,need%20to%20find%20hidden%20friends).

tute questions not covered

  • tut01, 02, 03Q1-Q3

item.title: Watamolla游记
item.description:
COVID还在继续……

因为觉得要是再不出去玩的话，整个人都要快被憋死了，所以上个周日决定去了悉尼周边的国家公园叫Royal National Park。澳洲一般国家公园都不收费，但估计开车去那儿的人太多了，所以他们收了$12的停车费。💸

国家公园很大，而且有好多景点。但这次就去了一个地方叫Watamolla。这个地方很特别的一点是，沙滩旁边有一个瀑布和幽静的树林，瀑布一般只有冬天能看到水，因为澳洲夏天天干物燥。海滩旁边的还有沿着海岸线悬崖建的绵延几十公里的步行栈道。那天我们走了近三个月来最多的路。一共来回大概十公里。海岸线的风光是没得说，有好多奇石，尤其有一个酷似鹰头，但一般澳洲悬崖上净是些带刺植物，对走栈道的人不是很友好。

走完回来坐在夕阳下的沙滩上，我们吃着昨晚剩的咖喱饭，欣赏着瀑布还是很惬意。最意想不到的是我们人生第一次看到纯野生海豹（下面有图）。看到的时候，公园工作人员已经来检查过了，并设了保护区域。这算第一次和真正野生动物的奇遇~ 🌊
